ecoli2_s42.note: Only 13 balls; kNN graph too sparse for stable R_opp

ionosphere_s0.note: Near-zero reciprocal support on high-comp minority; corrections nearly wipe CA weight

vehicle0_s1.note: Moderate R_opp but sparse n_opp and strong minority suppression

strongest_patterns: Sparse granulation destabilizes R_opp: adversarial runs have far fewer balls (13-51 vs 52-551) and downweighted balls see mean n_opp=2.3 vs 10.1 in successful runs. With k=5 on <30 balls, reciprocal-opposite counts become noisy; ecoli2 (13 balls) and ionosphere (27) show the worst corrections (mean |Topo-CA|=0.51-0.84). spambase (551 balls) stabilizes R_opp at 0.77 with rich kNN connectivity.

R_opp=0 causes catastrophic downweighting on high-competition balls: 31.6% of high-compA downweighted balls in adversarial runs have R_opp=0 (vs 2.2% successful), producing mean |Topo-CA|~1.0 (full CA weight removal). ionosphere_s0 is the extreme case (hcm |Topo-CA|=1.16). Useful corrections require non-zero reciprocal support; zero R_opp is not selective noise suppression but total ball silencing.

Harmful corrections are larger in magnitude, not driven by purity/radius: purity is ~1.0 in both groups; radius and ball_size do not separate outcomes. Instead, adversarial runs apply mean |Topo-CA|=0.55 on corrected balls vs 0.34 successful, with high-comp minority balls penalized nearly 2x harder (-0.83 vs -0.46 mean Topo-CA). R_opp helps when downweighting is moderate (high mean R_opp ~0.76); it hurts when the same compA balls get R_opp near 0 or corrections are oversized relative to CA.
hypothesis_for_future_modification: R_opp is informative only when the ball graph is sufficiently dense (n_balls >> k) and reciprocal opposite support is non-degenerate. Principled modification would need to guard against R_opp=0 total suppression on high-compA minority balls and/or down-weight R_opp when granulation is sparse. Not proposed or implemented here.
